originalTitle: Hyperscaler debt signals warning sign, Apollo cautions
summary: Credit default swaps for companies building data centers are getting pricier, and it's not because banks are hedging more of their bets.
content:
Corporate debt issued by the giant cloud computing players powering the artificial intelligence boom is getting riskier, private equity firm Apollo Global Management warned on Wednesday.

Risk insurance contracts, known as credit default swaps, or CDS, for bonds issued by hyperscalers are getting pricier, and it's not because banks are hedging more of their bets as bond issuance climbs, Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok wrote in a Wednesday note .

"What the market is repricing is hyperscaler credit fundamentals, namely a debt-financed AI capex cycle with rising leverage, negative free cash flow and uncertain payback on depreciating assets," Slok wrote.

If dealer hedging of new bonds were responsible for the rise in risk insurance prices, that widening would show up in the issuers of those bonds — the banks. But that's not what's happening.

The gap between hyperscaler CDS and bank CDS has widened to around 60 basis points from roughly 0 since October of 2025, implying that hyperscaler credit risk is increasing on its own terms, Slok's research shows.

The note from Apollo follows warnings from the leaders of frontier, large language models over the weekend, who said they want to slow the rate of advancements of their products due to safety concerns. That could have financial consequences for the cloud computing providers that run the LLMs.

Many folks on Wall Street think the frontier model companies are seeking regulation from Washington that can protect them from competition from startups, and guard against legal liability for the actions of autonomous agents.

"What I believe they're really shooting for is the Communications Act treatment that protected the social media guys," Dan Alpert, founding managing partner of Westwood Capital, said. "They want some legislation that 'regulates' them, but what it really does is absolves them."

Section 230 of the Communications Act of 1996 specifies "internet platforms would not be treated as publishers of third-party content" and that "platforms would not be held liable for user-posted content," according to the National Association of Attorneys General .

"The banks have built up … fortress balance sheets … They have built up a significant equity buffer and they are now much more highly diversified in their exposure than they were during the mortgage crisis," Alpert said. "That is where the answer may lie in terms of the way the market is looking at the credit risk."

Technology investors say margins for the hyperscalers are increasing, justifying the debt issuance, and that it's too soon to worry about the widening CDS spreads.

"[Hyperscalers] don't really add their capacity in a significant enough way into 2027 and 2028 to know how this is going to turn out," Paul Meeks, head of technology research at Freedom Capital Markets, said. "We're starting to see a turn to the positive in their margins, and if we continue to see [this], there will be less concerns."

Alphabet has a forward debt-to-equity ratio of 13% and forward free cash flow of negative $25.7 billion, according to FactSet.

Amazon has debt-to-equity of 23% and free cash flow of negative $30 billion. Meta Platforms has debt-to equity of 34% and free cash flow of negative $25.7 billion. Microsoft has debt-to-equity of 7.34% and positive free cash flow of $33.4 billion.

Economists are also keeping a close eye on the credit conditions of the hyperscalers in light of the Wednesday warning on credit default swaps from Apollo.

"The issue here is that CDS investors, who are the most sophisticated investors anywhere (possibly wrong, but definitely in the weeds), are attaching far greater risk to the debt of the most profitable companies in the world," Dean Baker, founder of the Center for Economic and Policy Research, said. "They obviously think there is a substantial risk that the AI companies cannot make good on their commitments."
chineseTitle: 阿波罗警告称，超大规模债务发出了警告信号
chineseSummary: 建设数据中心的公司的信用违约掉期价格越来越高，这并不是因为银行正在对冲更多的赌注。
chineseContent:
私募股权公司阿波罗全球管理公司周三警告称，推动人工智能热潮的云计算巨头发行的企业债务风险正变得越来越大。

阿波罗首席经济学家托斯顿·斯洛克(Torsten Slok)在周三的一份报告中写道，超大规模企业发行的债券的风险保险合约（称为信用违约互换（CDS））价格越来越高，这并不是因为随着债券发行量的增加，银行正在对冲更多的赌注。

斯洛克写道：“市场正在重新定价的是超大规模信贷基本面，即债务融资的人工智能资本支出周期，杠杆率不断上升，自由现金流为负，资产贬值的回报不确定。”

如果交易商对新债券的对冲是风险保险价格上涨的原因，那么这种扩大将体现在这些债券的发行人——银行身上。但事实并非如此。

Slok 的研究显示，自 2025 年 10 月以来，超大规模企业 CDS 与银行 CDS 之间的差距已从大约 0 扩大到约 60 个基点，这意味着超大规模企业信用风险本身正在增加。

Apollo 的说明是在周末前沿大型语言模型的领导者发出警告之后发出的，他们表示出于安全考虑，他们希望放慢其产品的进步速度。这可能会对运行法学硕士的云计算提供商产生财务影响。

华尔街的许多人认为，前沿模范公司正在寻求华盛顿的监管，以保护它们免受初创公司的竞争，并防止对自主代理的行为承担法律责任。

Westwood Capital 的创始管理合伙人丹·阿尔珀特 (Dan Alpert) 表示：“我认为他们真正想要的是保护社交媒体人士的《通信法》待遇。” “他们想要一些‘监管’他们的立法，但它真正的作用是赦免他们。”

根据国家总检察长协会的说法，1996 年《通信法》第 230 条规定“互联网平台不得被视为第三方内容的发布者”，并且“平台不对用户发布的内容承担责任”。

阿尔珀特表示：“银行已经建立了……堡垒式的资产负债表……他们已经建立了重要的股权缓冲，而且现在的风险敞口比抵押贷款危机期间更加多元化。” “这可能就是市场看待信用风险的方式的答案。”

科技投资者表示，超大规模企业的利润正在增加，证明了发债的合理性，而且现在担心 CDS 利差扩大还为时过早。

Freedom Capital Markets 技术研究主管 Paul Meeks 表示：“到 2027 年和 2028 年，[超大规模企业] 并没有真正以足够大的方式增加其容量，因此无法知道结果如何。” “我们开始看到他们的利润率出现积极变化，如果我们继续看到这种情况，担忧就会减少。”

FactSet 的数据显示，Alphabet 的远期债务股本率为 13%，远期自由现金流为负 257 亿美元。

亚马逊的债务股本率为 23%，自由现金流为负 300 亿美元。 Meta Platforms 的债务股本率为 34%，自由现金流为负 257 亿美元。微软的债务股本率为 7.34%，自由现金流为 334 亿美元。

鉴于阿波罗周三对信用违约掉期发出的警告，经济学家也在密切关注超大规模企业的信用状况。

经济与政策研究中心创始人迪恩·贝克 (Dean Baker) 表示：“这里的问题是，CDS 投资者是世界上最老练的投资者（可能是错误的，但绝对是杂草），他们给世界上最赚钱的公司的债务带来了更大的风险。” “他们显然认为人工智能公司存在无法兑现承诺的巨大风险。”
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
